title: Constraining the Volume Density of Dusty Star-forming Galaxies through the First 3 mm Number Counts from ALMA
question: What are the 3 mm galaxy number counts from archival ALMA Band 3 data, and what do they imply for the volume density of DSFGs and their contribution to the CSFRD at z>4?

what.value: Backward evolution model of the submm sky (IRLF evolution, SED assignment) used for predictions

evidence.loc: 4 Constraining the infrared galaxy luminosity function
evidence.quote: we use the estimated galaxy number counts and the predictions from the backward evolution model presented by (cite: Casey2018a; Casey2018b)

recipe.method: Query ALMA archive for Band 3 data in UDS, CDF-S, COSMOS with resolution and sensitivity cuts
SNR maps from uncorrected PB maps, noise = 68th percentile of pixels, 5 sigma threshold, iterative masking
key_parameters: threshold 5 sigma; radius 1.3 x primary beam FWHM
assumptions: Fluxes scaled to 3 mm with S proportional to nu^(2+beta), beta=1.8

recipe.method: Inverted maps for false detections; Monte Carlo source injection (100 realizations per SNR bin)
N_i=(1-f_cont)/(zeta A_eff) summed; Monte Carlo and Poisson errors; double power law fit
Fit model number counts for psi2 (-6.5 to -2.0) and z_cutoff (9 to 5) by maximum likelihood with flat priors
assumptions: Optically thick SEDs at rest-frame lambda<100 um

evidence.quote: This compilation covers an effective area of $198\,\rm arcmin^2$

evidence.loc: 4 Constraining the infrared galaxy luminosity function

answer_key.quantity: DSFG share of CSFRD at z~4-5

evidence.loc: 4 Constraining the infrared galaxy luminosity function
evidence.quote: DSFGs contribute $\approx35-85\%$ of the total CSFRD at $z\approx4-5$
a false detection rate of $\lesssim5\%$ is expected at our adopted threshold
